newsitem.title: ITALY: Mediaset to decide on Telepiu stake end-Jan.
newsitem.headline: Mediaset to decide on Telepiu stake end-Jan.

text.p: Italian television and advertising group Mediaset will decide at its end-January board meeting whether to exercise an option to buy the 10 percent stake in Italian pay-TV group Telepiu held by its parent company Fininvest Spa.

Mediaset chairman Fedele Confalonieri, replying to reporters' questions as to when the decision would be taken, said: "At the end of the month there is the Mediaset board meeting." Mediaset sources said no date had yet been fixed.

When Mediaset announced in December that it had exercised options to buy 25 percent stakes in three Spanish television companies from Fininvest it also said at the time it would decide on the Telepiu stake at the January board meeting.

The Milan daily Corriere della Sera reported on Thursday that Mediaset's bank partners were not keen on the company taking a direct stake in Telepiu because they reckon the pay-TV has, and will continue to have for some years, large financing needs and no profits.
Also, the newspaper said, global developments in the sector and especially the merger between Nethold, a Telepiu shareholder, with Canal Plus could herald changes in the shareholding structure.

Industry sources said that Nethold and the German Kirch group currently each hold 45 percent of Telepiu but if this setup changed Mediaset, with its possible 10 percent, might have problems facing up to a group controlling 90 percent.
After the flotation of Mediaset on the Milan bourse last summer, former prime minister Silvio Berlusconi's Fininvest controls some 50 percent of Mediaset.
Mediaset shares were some four percent up at 7,290 lire on a firmer Milan bourse at 1515 GMT.
